what: BNY is a custody bank. It holds and administers assets for institutions, settles trades, handles corporate bond payments and manages money. It does not lend much; it is paid to safeguard and process.
customers: Asset managers, pension funds, insurers, governments, corporations and wealthy families.
money: custody, fund accounting and asset servicing
managing investments for institutions and wealthy clients
moat: Trillions of dollars of assets sitting in its custody systems, which are deeply embedded in clients' operations and very rarely moved.
risks: Fee income falls when markets fall, because fees are charged on asset values
Interest income depends on rates and on clients leaving cash with it
Custody is a low-margin, price-competitive business
Operational errors in settlement can be costly
opportunities: A multi-year programme is cutting costs and lifting its return on equity
Digital assets and tokenised funds need an established custodian, a role it is pursuing
Capital returns through buybacks have been steady
watch: Fee revenue growth against expenses, which determines whether operating leverage is improving.
